extracted.intended_audience: advanced students and researchers in classical mechanics and mathematical physics (readers of Newtonian dynamics)
extracted.subtask_description: Geometric and analytic rules for determining projectile trajectories (parabolas, hyperbolas, spirals) in media with specified resistance laws, and constructions to recover medium density or curve from observed motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for parabolic motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion occurs in a parabola only when the medium does not resist; if the medium is non-resisting the projectile describes a parabola (as Galileo demonstrated), otherwise the path is hyperbolic under continuous resistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholium: If the medium offers no resistance then the trajectory is a parabola. When resistance is present and appropriate, the actual path approaches hyperbolas of the kinds described; those hyperbolas may be used as practical approximations to observed trajectories, with more composite hyperbolas sometimes more useful in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 1 — invariance of AH, AI, HX under change of angle at fixed density
rubrics_metrics.description: If the medium density at A is held constant and the angle NAH is changed, the lengths AH, AI, HX remain unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, if density at a point is fixed, varying the launch angle (NAH) does not change these characteristic lengths; so knowing these lengths determines aspects of the hyperbola independent of angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 2 — inverse-square dependence of AI on speed when density fixed
rubrics_metrics.description: If both the angle NAH and the medium density at A are fixed and the projectile speed is changed, AH is preserved and AI changes in the duplicate (square) ratio reciprocally to the speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically AI varies inversely as the square of the speed; hence doubling speed reduces AI by factor 4. Useful for scaling constructions when velocity is altered but medium/density is held constant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 3 — proportional change of AH:AI with change in resistance-to-gravity ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If angle NAH, projectile velocity in A, and the accelerating gravity are held fixed, but the proportion of resistance to driving gravity in A is increased by any ratio, the proportion AH:AI increases in the same ratio (with corresponding quadratic relation AH^2:AI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing the ratio resistive_force:gravity scales AH relative to AI; as a result AH decreases in the same ratio and AI decreases in its duplicate ratio. Also indicates how changes in specific gravity, medium density or resistance magnitude alter AH and AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 4 — correction for nonuniform density near vertex using tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: Because medium density near the hyperbola's vertex is greater than at point A, to preserve the mean (average) density one must find the ratio of the smallest tangent GT to the tangent at AH, and diminish the density at A by a little less than the semisum of tangents divided by tangent AH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a geometrical correction to account for local density variation near the vertex when applying hyperbola constructions to experimental data; use the relation of tangents to adjust the assumed density at A (see following Regs for how to apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 5 — construction of hyperbola from given AH and AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Given lengths AH and AI, to describe the curve AGK: extend HN to X so that HX equals the product (n+1) & AI (construction depends on chosen exponent n); with center X and asymptotes MX, NX through A, describe the hyperbola so that AI : any VG = XV^n : XI^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a geometric construction rule to draw the hyperbola passing through A given AH, AI and a chosen index n that controls the asymptotic law VG ∝ DN^-n. Follow the specified proportional relations between AI, VG and powers of segments XV, XI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 6 — choice of exponent n affects accuracy above/below vertex
rubrics_metrics.description: The larger the chosen number n, the more accurate these hyperbolas are for the ascending portion of the projectile from A, and the less accurate for the descending portion toward G (and vice versa). Conic (n special) hyperbola gives moderate compromise and is simpler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose n according to whether one needs accuracy on ascent or descent; for practical mechanical use, keep AH and AI constant across angles (Reg. 1–3) and apply Reg. 4 corrections if greater accuracy is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 7 — experimental determination of hyperbola from two projectile firings
rubrics_metrics.description: Project two identical bodies with equal velocities at two different angles; record the impact distances AK and Ak, and take their ratio d:e. Erect perpendiculars AI (arbitrary length AH or Ah), then graphically determine AK, Ak by Reg. 6; if AK:Ak equals d:e the assumed AH was correct, otherwise adjust graphically using difference and repeat until obtaining AH equal to true value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a practical experimental/graphical method to recover AH (and thereby the hyperbola) from measured ranges at two angles. It prescribes constructing perpendiculars, comparing measured ratios, and adjusting by drawing a corrective perpendicular proportional to the difference between measured and expected ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reg. 8 — geometric construction to find launch line AH for given target K
rubrics_metrics.description: Given AH and HX, to locate the position of line AH such that a projectile launched at that speed hits a given point K: erect perpendiculars AC and KF to the horizon at A and K, set AC downward equal to AI (= ½ HX), then describe the hyperbola with asymptotes AK and KF whose conjugate passes through C; the intersection H of that hyperbola with the circle centered A of radius AH gives the correct launch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives explicit geometric steps (construct perpendiculars, set AC = ½HX = AI, draw hyperbola with appropriate conjugate through C, intersect with circle of radius AH) to determine the required launch line AH geometrically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XI (Theor. VIII) — velocities geometric under mixed resistance with arithmetic time
rubrics_metrics.description: If a body is resisted partly in the ratio of velocity and partly in the duplicate ratio of velocity (i.e., resistance ~ v + v^2), and the sole propelling force is the innate vis of the medium, and times are taken in arithmetic progression, then quantities reciprocally proportional to the velocities are in geometric progression (equivalently: velocities grow/decay so that their reciprocals form a geometric progression).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates via hyperbolic-area representation that when resistance = a*v + b*v^2 and time increments are equal, 1/v decreases proportionally and composes with a fixed quantity CG so that CD grows in geometric progression; corollaries indicate one can represent velocity by the reciprocal 1/GD where GD composes with a fixed CG to form CD in geometric progression, allowing graphical/area methods to find velocity from time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollaries to Prop. XI — velocity from hyperbolic area and locating G
rubrics_metrics.description: Corol.1: If times are represented by equal hyperbolic areas ABED, then velocity can be represented by the reciprocal 1/GD. Corol.2: Taking GA : GD as initial reciprocal velocity to final reciprocal velocity yields point G; once G is found velocity at any other time is found similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives practical method to obtain velocities from time by hyperbolic-area / reciprocal-length constructions described in the proposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XII (Theor. IX) — spaces arithmetic imply velocities geometric under mixed resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the same hypotheses (resistance ~ v + v^2), if the spaces described are taken in arithmetic progression, then velocities (when increased by a certain given quantity) are in geometric progression; velocity can be represented by length GD which with given CG composes CD in a geometric progression while space increases arithmetically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the dual representation to Prop. XI: representing space by hyperbolic areas yields velocity-length GD; corollaries give means to find G and then deduce space from given velocity and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XIII (Theor. X) — times as sector areas for motion under uniform gravity and mixed resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a body moves up or down under uniform gravity along a straight line and is resisted partly proportional to v and partly to v^2, and only the innate vis moves it, then if lines parallel to conjugate diameters are drawn and velocities are proportional to certain segments, the times of motion are proportional to the areas of the corresponding sectors (and conversely).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives three cases: (1) when resistance law matches circle-quadrant geometry, time is proportional to a circular sector; (2) when hyperbola arises, time is hyperbolic sector; (3) in descent case similar hyperbolic sector result. The proposition maps physical laws (gravity + mixed resistance) to geometric area representations that yield elapsed times and so provide constructions to compute times from geometrical areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XIV (Prob. IV) — space of ascent/descent as sum/difference of areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the same hypotheses and that composite forces from resistance and gravity sum geometrically, the space described in ascent or descent is equal to the sum or difference of the area through which time is represented and another area which increases or decreases in arithmetic progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a formulaic/area-based method to obtain the distance ascended/descended using moments of areas: build area AbNK whose momenta combine with sector DET to yield the spatial momenta. Cases elaborate how to set the auxiliary line AC proportional to gravity and resistance combinations and thereby compute the space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma III — geometric relation for a spiral cutting all radii at equal angles
rubrics_metrics.description: For a logarithmic-type spiral PQRr cutting all radii SP,SQ,SR at equal angles: if PT is tangent at P cutting SQ in T, and perpendiculars to the spiral at P and Q meet at O, then as P and Q approach, angle PSO tends to a right angle and the limiting ratio TQ × PS to PQ^2 is one of equality (i.e., PQ^2 = TQ × PS in the limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful geometric identity relating infinitesimal chord PQ, tangent segment TQ and radius PS for spirals cutting radii at constant angle. Employed in proofs about motion in spirals and in deriving relations between centripetal force, density and resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XV (Theor. XI) — spiral motion when medium density ∝ 1/distance and centripetal force ∝ density^2
rubrics_metrics.description: If medium density at each point is reciprocally proportional to the distance from a fixed center, and the centripetal force is in the duplicate ratio of density (i.e., centripetal ∝ density^2), then a body may revolve in a spiral which cuts all radii from the center at a given angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposition shows how, under the stated density law, times, velocities and resistances scale so that equal-area pieces correspond to equal time slices, leading to relations that fix the spiral. Corollaries give practical relations: velocity at P equals that for circular motion at same radius; density from given radius is proportional to OS/OP; the ratio of resistive to centripetal force is ½ OS : OP, and spirals can be adapted to given densities or vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XVI (Theor. XII) — generalization for density ∝ 1/distance^n
rubrics_metrics.description: If the medium density at each point is reciprocally proportional to some power n of the distance from the center (density ∝ 1/SP^n), and centripetal force ∝ distance^n, then a body can revolve in a spiral cutting each radius at a given angle; the density in P is reciprocally proportional to SP^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes Prop. XV to arbitrary power-law density/centripetal relations: time to describe arc PQ scales as PQ × SP^(n/2), resistance scales accordingly, and density law follows density ∝ 1/SP^n. Use the same geometric/infinitesimal reasoning as in Prop. XV but with exponent n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XVII (Prob. V) — problem: find centripetal force and medium resistance for given spiral motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a spiral PQR and the motion along it (arc increments and tangential data), one can find the centripetal force and the medium resistance such that the body will revolve in that given spiral under those forces and resistances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: from the known arc PQ and height TQ (which is proportional to centripetal force × time^2) and from area differences PSQ & QSR (which give retardation), compute retardation and deduce resistive force and medium density. The proposition is essentially an inverse construction: from observed geometric motion recover forces and density.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XVIII (Prob. VI) — problem: given centripetal law find medium density so body describes given spiral
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a law for the centripetal force, find the medium density at each location so that a body will describe a given spiral under that centripetal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: from the given centripetal force deduce local velocities, then from the velocities' retardation deduce density. This is the direct inverse of Prop. XVII and uses the constructions of Prop. XV–XVI and Lemma III.
